Getting in

Entry

Sign in

How you use it

Email and password. The panel on the left is not marketing — it states the three rules the build actually enforces, so the first thing anyone reads is what the system refuses to do.

What happens underneath

argon2id password hashing, a short-lived JWT access token and a rotating refresh token with family revocation: reusing an old refresh token invalidates the whole family rather than just that token.

Why it is built this way

Registration always assigns analyst. Nobody can self-assign a privileged role over HTTP, so the first admin is created by a local CLI that already proves machine and database access.

Entry

Public front door

How you use it

Reachable without an account. It reconstructs one nominated, completed investigation so an evaluator meets the system before meeting its login form.

What happens underneath

A single read-only endpoint reports what the pipeline already stored. Nothing is computed on demand — a public page that ran analysis would be a free compute endpoint pointed at the internet.

Why it is built this way

Vessel identity is withheld. Candidates appear as evidence strength only. Naming a real vessel on a public page, from a system whose own output is a lead rather than a verdict, would be an accusation.

Orientation

Orientation

Operations dashboard

How you use it

The landing screen after sign-in. Run verified Sentinel-1 demo sets up the reference incident in one click. The tiles link onward; the queue shows every job and its state.

What happens underneath

One request builds the whole page, scoped to what the caller can see — an analyst's tiles count their own cases, an admin's count the instance, and the page prints which.

Why it is built this way

The button performs setup only: find the investigation, locate the product in a live catalogue, queue the ingest. Detection, back-tracking and ranking are left to run live, because pre-computing them turns a demonstration into a playback.

Orientation

System status

How you use it

Seven capabilities, each AVAILABLE, DEGRADED, UNAVAILABLE or OPTIONAL, with the providers behind it and whether each is configured.

What happens underneath

Configuration plus recorded provider health — no live network probe, so it is safe to poll from every screen. Wind additionally reads the last recorded drift run rather than trusting that a key exists.

Why it is built this way

Every card carries a consequence, not just a state. An operator needs to know a credential is missing; an analyst needs to know a missing wind field under-displaces a wind-driven slick. The overall state is the weakest link, never an average.

Orientation

Investigations

How you use it

Filter by name, reference or status. Each card shows how far its chain got and what to do next.

What happens underneath

Per-stage counts come from one grouped aggregate per collection — four round trips for fifty rows, not two hundred.

Why it is built this way

A status field cannot answer the question you arrive with. DRAFT covers both a case made a minute ago and one whose ingest died three stages back; only the counts separate them.

Orientation

New investigation

How you use it

Name the case, pick an area — from named presets or a bounding box — and set a UTC window. Presets state AIS coverage before you commit to an area.

What happens underneath

The polygon is rewound to the right-hand rule before storage and its true geodesic area measured against a 50,000 km² ceiling.

Why it is built this way

Winding matters because MongoDB reads a clockwise exterior ring as the polygon's complement — the whole planet except your box. The AIS coverage note prevents the commonest wasted hour: a perfect detection somewhere no free AIS archive reaches.

The workspace

Workspace

The investigation workspace

How you use it

One screen for the whole chain. The map persists across tabs; the timeline scrubs vessel positions through the window at 1× to 300×.

What happens underneath

MapLibre for the basemap and raster tiles, deck.gl for tracks and origin surfaces. Land and coastlines are served locally from Natural Earth.

Why it is built this way

The Progress panel names the next step rather than leaving you to infer it, and positions the system cannot place honestly are omitted from the timeline rather than interpolated.

The chain

Stage 1

Find and ingest a scene

How you use it

Find acquisitions searches the catalogues for this investigation's own area and window and offers what came back — acquisition time, platform, orbit, AOI overlap. Pick one and ingest. Analysts holding their own imagery can upload a GeoTIFF instead.

What happens underneath

The scene is windowed to the AOI, written as a Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF to object storage, served as map tiles, and detection runs automatically.

Why it is built this way

Ingestibility is decided at search time. Three providers search; one serves products this pipeline can read. Acquisitions it cannot ingest are listed with the reason rather than dropped — discovering it at job time produced a 404 that read like an outage.

Stage 2

Review a detection

How you use it

Confirm, reject or edit each candidate. The dialog carries the four confidence terms with their raw values, morphology, backscatter and the full version history.

What happens underneath

The detector's own output is immutable. Version 0 is always what the model said; every human action is appended, never overwritten.

Why it is built this way

Detection is a candidate generator, not a classifier. On a held-out real split it overlaps every true slick and also fires on 68.2% of look-alike scenes — so review gates the rest of the chain rather than being optional.

Stage 3

Back-track to an origin

How you use it

Run the back-track on a confirmed detection. It returns a probable origin zone with 50% and 90% probability contours, and a release-time window.

What happens underneath

Particles are integrated backwards through a real Copernicus Marine current field, with the wind-drift coefficient and Ekman deflection sampled per particle rather than fixed.

Why it is built this way

Fixing those coefficients would give a tight, confident-looking blob whose precision is fictional. The language is probable origin and release window throughout — never exact origin or exact time.

Stage 4

AIS coverage and tracks

How you use it

Coverage is reported before anything else — record count, distinct vessels, median reporting interval, temporal completeness and a plain assessment of what that evidence base can support.

What happens underneath

Real NOAA Marine Cadastre positions in a time-series collection. In-band sentinels are neutralised on import: a speed of 102.3 knots means unknown, not a measurement. Envelope queries measure p95 84 ms at 9.4 million positions.

Why it is built this way

An attribution is only as good as the AIS beneath it. When there is none the system returns an explicit reason — no AIS evidence for this region and window — never an empty candidate list, because those are different claims.

Stage 5

Rank the candidates

How you use it

Ranked vessels, each with an evidence waterfall you can expand down to the individual AIS fixes behind any single feature. Weight sliders show how sensitive the ranking is to the weighting.

What happens underneath

Twelve features in three states — measured, missing, or not applicable — with weights renormalised over measured features only, and bootstrap confidence intervals.

Why it is built this way

A missing feature is never scored as zero: zero means no evidence in this dimension, missing means we could not look. Below six measured features the result is withheld regardless of score, and a degraded origin caps every candidate.

Stage 6

The investigation dossier

How you use it

Generates a paginated PDF, plus GeoJSON, CSV and a run manifest. Rendered server-side from the same route an analyst reads on screen.

What happens underneath

The document carries the methodology, every provenance record, and the uncertainty attached to each figure.

Why it is built this way

The Uncertainty and Provenance sections are structurally mandatory — the report cannot be generated without them. Everything the dossier does exists to produce a document someone can defend to a regulator.

Operating

Operating

Job activity

How you use it

Watch ingest, detection, drift and report jobs progress in real time, with the failed ones and their reasons kept visible.

What happens underneath

BullMQ with deterministic idempotency keys, so re-requesting the same work reuses the job rather than reading a provider twice. Progress is pushed over Socket.IO.

Why it is built this way

Failures stay in the history rather than being cleared. The dashboard queue in this report still shows jobs that failed against a wedged ML service — that record is how the cause was found.

Operating

Team and trail

How you use it

Add members with a per-investigation role, read the audit trail, and leave analyst notes on the case.

What happens underneath

Two independent gates gutter every scoped route: the global role, and the role on this investigation. Notes are immutable and retractable, author-only.

Why it is built this way

The audit log records what the system did; nothing recorded what a person thought. A log an administrator can edit is not evidence of anything, so there is no delete.

Operating

Administration

How you use it

Grant roles, watch live provider health and circuit state, read quota consumption, see every investigation with its per-stage counts, and download any rendered dossier.

What happens underneath

The investigations table flags a case whose owner was deleted; the dossier table flags an orphan — a rendered PDF whose investigation no longer exists.

Why it is built this way

An orphaned dossier is reachable through no scoped route, because there is no membership left to check. Listing it here is how real filed evidence stops being lost silently.

Operating

Orbital view

How you use it

See where every case sits. Marker size is total AOI area; selecting an incident moves the terminator to that incident's time.

What happens underneath

The night shading is the real solar terminator computed for the displayed instant, not a decorative gradient.

Why it is built this way

SAR sees through cloud and darkness, so a night overpass is normal. Showing the real terminator makes that legible instead of surprising.

Operating

In-product guide

How you use it

How to drive every feature and how each works underneath, reachable from the rail on any screen.

What happens underneath

Kept in step with the build, including the parts that reflect badly on it.

Why it is built this way

The guide states the detector's measured false-positive rate and the AIS coverage limit in the product itself. A limitation an operator can only discover by being surprised is a limitation the product is hiding.

Operating

Light theme

How you use it

Toggle from the top bar on any screen, including before sign-in.

What happens underneath

Both palettes are defined as tokens and applied at the document root before first paint, so there is no flash of the wrong theme.

Why it is built this way

The workspace is read in a dark room and on a lit projector. Applying the theme at the root rather than inside the app shell is what lets the sign-in screen honour it too.

What this system does not do

These are stated in the product itself, not only here. A limitation an operator can only discover by being surprised is a limitation the product is hiding.

It produces leads, not verdicts.
The output is a ranked investigative lead with its evidence and its uncertainty. Scores are uncalibrated: comparable between candidates in one report, and not between reports.
The detector fires on look-alike scenes.
Measured on 66 held-out real scenes it overlaps every true slick — and also fires on 68.2% of look-alike scenes, with its own warning channel reading only 0.26 on those errors. A parameter sweep over 384 scenes confirmed thresholds, area, shape and risk gates cannot fix it.
Wind is unconfirmed.
The Climate Data Store key authenticates, but ERA5 returns 403 licences not accepted until the dataset terms are accepted once. Until then the wind-drift term is zero and the drift run says so.
AIS covers US waters only.
The free bulk archive is NOAA Marine Cadastre. Elsewhere imagery and detection still work and the candidate list is empty for want of receivers, not vessels.
VARUNA — Vessel Attribution through Remote-sensing & Unified Navigational Analytics. Screenshots captured from the running stack at 1500×950.
